profile.reading: Skybox Chicago I sits at 800 East Devon Avenue, Elk Grove Village, Illinois 60007, near O'Hare International Airport in the Chicago metro area. The operator's own dedicated page for this facility describes 30 megawatts of capacity across 190,000 square feet on a 10 acre campus, with power density options ranging from 275 to 340 watts per square foot depending on redundancy tier, and states the facility is available now. The operator's own site describes ownership as Skybox Powered by Prologis, a joint venture with Prologis, a large publicly traded industrial and logistics real estate company; no independent second source corroborating this specific joint venture structure was found, though the statement comes directly from the operator's own site. Skybox Datacenters develops what it calls PowerCampus facilities, purpose built high density data centers with private onsite substations, with completed projects in Houston, Santa Clara, California, and Northern Virginia alongside this Chicago site, and projects underway in Austin, Dallas, and Wichita Falls, Texas. The Chicago facility carries LEED certification. Elk Grove Village sits in a well established Chicago area data center corridor near O'Hare, home to other major carrier hotel and colocation buildings including 350 East Cermak downtown, tracked elsewhere in this registry, though this suburban location offers lower real estate costs and large contiguous parcels better suited to purpose built wholesale campuses than downtown high rise carrier hotels. No founding date or headquarters address for Skybox Datacenters itself was located in available sourcing this session. The 189,000 square foot building was developed as a joint project between Skybox Datacenters and industrial real estate giant Prologis, completed in May 2022 on a 10 acre parcel at 800 E. Devon Avenue. The project was notable as an adaptive reuse effort, converting a vacant distribution warehouse into purpose built data center space rather than new ground up construction, reflecting a broader pattern of Chicago area data center developers repurposing industrial real estate near the citys fiber and power infrastructure. The building was constructed on a speculative basis, designed with the flexibility to serve either a single large tenant or multiple smaller colocation customers, with active leasing underway at the time of completion.

profile.reading: Skybox Houston One sits at 22000 Franz Road, Houston, Texas 77449, in Harris County. The operator's own dedicated page for this facility describes 26 megawatts of capacity across 96,129 square feet on a 20 acre private campus, engineered with a 6 inch concrete roof deck able to sustain winds over 190 miles per hour, reflecting the Gulf Coast's hurricane exposure, and DoubleDense technology supporting power densities up to 1,000 watts per square foot using immersion cooling for high density compute workloads. The operator's own site describes ownership as Skybox Powered by Prologis, a joint venture with Prologis, a large publicly traded industrial and logistics real estate company; no independent second source corroborating this specific joint venture structure was found, though the statement comes directly from the operator's own site. Skybox Datacenters develops what it calls PowerCampus facilities, purpose built high density data centers with private onsite substations, with completed projects in Chicago, Santa Clara, California, and Northern Virginia alongside this Houston site, and projects underway in Austin, Dallas, and Wichita Falls, Texas. The Houston facility carries LEED certification. Houston's data center market has grown substantially in recent years, drawing both traditional colocation and increasingly high density AI and HPC focused developers like Skybox, supported by the region's relatively low power costs on the ERCOT grid and proximity to the Gulf Coast's subsea cable landing infrastructure. No founding date or headquarters address for Skybox Datacenters itself was located in available sourcing this session. Skybox broke ground on the facility in July 2014 with completion targeted for that November, on a 20 acre campus in Katy, Texas within Houstons Energy Corridor, chosen for its access to the citys Interstate 10 fiber optic backbone. The roughly 87,000 square foot building was designed to open with four private 10,000 square foot data halls with room to expand to 12 halls across the full campus, drawing power from an adjacent 300MW electric utility substation on a dual feed A/B configuration with underground concrete encased duct banks. The building was built to LEED Silver standard with an FM I-150 rated roof system engineered to withstand 190 mph hurricane winds, reflecting the storm resilience requirements common to Gulf Coast data center construction.

reading:
Skybox Datacenters is a privately held data centre developer headquartered in Dallas, Texas, founded in 2014 by Rob Morris, who is chief executive, and Travis Young, who is chief financial officer. Skybox is a developer first and an operator second. Its stated product, which it calls PowerCampus, is end to end site selection, design and construction of large power dense campuses delivered as turnkey buildings, build to suit projects or powered shell, with a sister entity, Skybox Critical Operations, running facilities once they are built. The company says it has developed more than 2.5 gigawatts of projects across North America and lists activity in Dallas, Austin, Houston and Wichita Falls in Texas, plus Chicago, Northern Virginia, Santa Clara and San Francisco. Skybox does not publish its capitalisation, investors or ownership structure, and as a private company it files nothing with the SEC, so the 2.5 gigawatt figure is a company claim rather than an audited or filed number.

The registry holds two Skybox sites. Skybox Chicago I sits at 800 East Devon Avenue in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, a village that has become one of the densest data centre submarkets in the Midwest. Skybox publishes 190,000 square feet on a ten acre campus, LEED Silver certification, and dedicated dual 34.5 kilovolt services delivered by ComEd from the Itasca substation. Its capacity disclosure is unusually careful and worth reading precisely. Skybox states 30 megawatts of total utility load for the building, then separately states what the building supports as critical load depending on how much redundancy a tenant buys, 18 megawatts at 4N/3, 20 megawatts at 6N/5 and 22 megawatts at 12N/11. The 30 megawatt number is the service the building can draw. The 18 to 22 megawatt range is what actually reaches computing equipment. Directories that reprint a single Chicago I capacity figure are usually reprinting the utility number.

Chicago I also shows how Skybox's model ends. The building was a Prologis warehouse converted under a joint venture between Prologis and Skybox, and in December 2024 the completed asset was sold to HMC Capital for its DigiCo Infrastructure REIT, the second joint venture asset the two partners had sold. Skybox develops and exits rather than holding long term, which is why its facility count in any registry lags its stated development pipeline.

Skybox Houston One sits on a twenty acre private campus in Harris County, Texas, at 96,129 square feet with 26 megawatts of capacity and a range of 120 to 600 watts per square foot, up to 480 watts air cooled or 1,000 watts with immersion. Skybox describes a loop fed 400 megavolt ampere substation with dual underground utility service and an adjacent 300 megavolt ampere substation, which is transformer capacity on the grid rather than anything the building draws. Standby generation is separate again, listed as 2.0 megawatt generators with 7,000 gallon belly tanks giving 96 hours of fuel. The building is LEED Gold with a six inch concrete roof deck rated for winds above 190 miles per hour, a Gulf Coast design choice, and Skybox aims it at oil and gas and high performance computing tenants.
